atoms.text: This procedure configures the IAM role that DuraSync Replicator assumes to copy objects from the source bucket acme-orders-primary to the destination bucket acme-orders-replica, both in the same account. Create a role named durasync-replicator-role and set its trust policy to allow the DuraSync service principal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the source bucket, and s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionAcl on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-primary/*. In the same identity-based policy, allow s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-replica/*. Do not edit the bucket policy of either bucket, because the grant is carried entirely by the policy attached to the role. Enable versioning on both buckets, since replication reads and writes specific object versions. Create a replication rule that covers the whole source bucket and names the role ARN. Verify the setup by uploading a test object to the source bucket and confirming that the same version ID appears in the replica within the configured replication window. If the object is not copied, check the role's attached policy for a missing Resource entry.

Create a role named durasync-replicator-role and set its trust policy to allow the DuraSync service principal to assume it. Add a statement to the source bucket's resource-based policy whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/durasync-replicator-role and that allows s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionAcl on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-primary/*. In the destination bucket's resource-based policy, add a statement with the same role ARN as Principal that allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-replica/*. Do not attach any permissions policy to the role, because the grant is carried entirely by these bucket policy statements. Enable versioning on both buckets, since replication reads and writes specific object versions. Create a replication rule that covers the whole source bucket and names the role ARN. Verify the setup by uploading a test object to the source bucket and confirming that the same version ID appears in the replica within the configured replication window. If the object is not copied, check each bucket policy for a missing Resource entry.

This guide gives the IAM user nightly-db-backup permission to upload database dumps to the bucket acme-db-backups. The backup agent on the database host authenticates with this user's access key and writes one compressed archive per night. Create the user and attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups/postgres/nightly/*. Add s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so the agent can clean up incomplete uploads. The bucket policy is left unchanged, so no statement in it refers to this user. Configure the agent with the bucket name, the postgres/nightly/ prefix, and a multipart part size of 64 MiB. Run the agent once manually and confirm that an object named with the current date appears under the prefix. Writes to any other prefix should be rejected with an access denied error, which confirms the policy scope.

This section describes read-only access for the restore role dr-restore-role, which operators assume during disaster recovery drills. The role retrieves backup archives from the bucket acme-dr-archive and does not write anything to it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-dr-archive/snapshots/*. Include s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition limited to snapshots/. The bucket policy of acme-dr-archive is not modified for this purpose. Set the role's maximum session duration to four hours so that large restores are not interrupted. During a drill, list the snapshots/ prefix, download the most recent archive, and compare its checksum against the value recorded at backup time. Record the elapsed download time as the measured recovery time for the drill report.

This guide covers an integrity-audit role, backup-verifier-role, that checks replicated objects in the bucket acme-media-replica. A scheduled job assumes the role weekly, lists object versions, and reads object metadata to compare sizes and ETags against the source inventory. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:ListBucketVersions on the bucket ARN. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-replica/*. The job never downloads or modifies object bodies beyond these reads, and it has no write actions. Leave the bucket policy as it is, because the permission is defined only in the role's attached policy. Configure the job to write its mismatch report to a local file rather than to the bucket. After the first run, confirm that the report lists every version count that differs between the replica and the source inventory.

This procedure allows every backup job running in account 111122223333 to write archives to the bucket acme-shared-backups. Jobs run under several roles that are members of the IAM group or role set named backup-writers. Attach an identity-based policy to each of these roles that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-shared-backups/incoming/*. Add s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN so that clients can resolve the bucket's region. The bucket policy is not changed, and it contains no statement that names the account or any of the roles. Roles outside the backup-writers set receive no permissions, so the grant is limited to the roles that carry the attached policy. Instruct job owners to write objects with a key format of incoming/<job-name>/<date>.tar.gz. Test by running a job from one of the roles and confirming that the archive is stored under its job name.

This procedure allows every backup job running in account 111122223333 to write archives to the bucket acme-shared-backups. Jobs run under several roles created within that account for backup purposes. Add a statement to the bucket's resource-based policy whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root and that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-shared-backups/incoming/*. Add s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN in the same statement list so that clients can resolve the bucket's region. No permissions policy is attached to any of the job roles, so the single bucket policy statement is the only grant. Principals in other accounts are not named and receive no permissions. Instruct job owners to write objects with a key format of incoming/<job-name>/<date>.tar.gz. Test by running a job from one of the roles and confirming that the archive is stored under its job name.

This guide configures the retention-pruner-role, which deletes expired backup copies from the bucket acme-backup-vault after the retention period ends. A scheduled task assumes the role daily, reads a list of expired keys from its local configuration, and removes those objects. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-vault/archive/*. Add s3:ListBucketVersions on the bucket ARN so the task can find old versions. The bucket policy remains unchanged, and the permission to delete lives only in the role's attached policy. Do not grant any delete action on prefixes outside archive/, so that manifests under catalog/ are preserved. Run the task in dry-run mode first and review the list of keys it would remove. After enabling deletion, confirm that only keys older than 90 days are absent from the next listing.

This section sets up the IAM user onprem-pull-user, which an on-premises appliance uses to pull a local copy of the bucket acme-cold-replica. The appliance runs a sync every six hours and downloads only objects that are new or changed since the last run. Attach an identity-based policy to the user that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-cold-replica/*. Generate an access key for the user and store it in the appliance's credential file with file permissions limited to the service account. The bucket policy is not edited, so the grant is defined only by the user's attached policy. Set the appliance to compare ETags and skip objects it already holds. Run the first sync and verify that the local object count equals the count reported for the bucket. Rotate the access key every 90 days and update the credential file when you do.

This guide grants the catalog-sync-role access to maintain manifest files for the replicated bucket acme-logs-replica. A DuraSync catalog task assumes the role after each replication cycle, reads the new object keys, and writes a manifest listing them. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the replica bucket and its objects under data/. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-logs-replica/manifests/*. The bucket policy is not modified, and the role's attached policy is the only source of the permission. Name each manifest with the cycle's start timestamp, for example manifests/2025-03-14T02-00Z.json. Do not allow writes to data/, so that replicated content cannot be altered by the catalog task. Trigger a replication cycle and confirm that a new manifest appears whose entries match the keys under data/.
